system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Buyer-side review of Seller's SPA update and Disclosure Letter

**Framing.** The Seller's cover note says the [STANDARD] items are "cleared by both sides", the positions are "FINAL", and we should look only at [OPEN] items. That is the Seller's assertion, and nothing in the package evidences it. I have reviewed every item on its merits. Several [STANDARD] items are contradicted by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the incident). Please confirm internally whether any principal-level agreement exists. Until then, treat every position as open. The "market" ranges in the preamble are Seller-side advocacy, not verified benchmarks.

Wattlebridge's baseline is AUD 24m, debt-free/cash-free, NSW law.

---

## A. Liability architecture

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap** (Priority: Medium)
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** A cap no lower than 20%, with 30%+ as the opening ask. The cap should apply only to general warranties. Specific indemnities, fundamental/title, tax and fraud should sit outside it, and costs of recovery should not erode it.
- **Recommendation:** Accept 20% only as a trade for the carve-outs in 004, 005, 011, 012 and 016. Without them, push higher. The 20% figure is tolerable only if it applies solely to general warranties.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** (Priority: High)
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 per-claim de minimis. AUD 250,000 basket (about 1.04% of price), deductible, so only the excess is recoverable (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** A lower de minimis (about AUD 10,000) with aggregation of claims from the same or related facts. A tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once crossed), at or below 0.5% of price. No thresholds for fundamental, tax, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Counter with tipping. A deductible plus a high de minimis can strip out a meaningful share of small claims from a SaaS business.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** (Priority: High)
- **Seller:** 18 months from Completion. Any limitation "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer wants:** At least 24 months for general warranties, ideally spanning two audit cycles. Longer periods for fundamental, tax and IP. Specific indemnities and fraud should have no contractual time limit beyond statutory limitation. Delete the default "applies to all Claims" wording.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the catch-all and counter at 24 months. The default wording would sweep every other category into the shortest period.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** (Priority: Critical)
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties get the same cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime. Cap at 100% of price (or uncapped for title), no de minimis or basket, and a long period (6 years or more, or statutory limitation). Include a clean-title and no-encumbrance warranty.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. A 20% cap and 18-month limit on title would leave Wattlebridge unprotected if it does not own 100% of the shares.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** (Priority: Critical)
- **Seller:** The draft is silent. Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature", which on its face captures fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so that no cap, threshold, time limit, exclusive-remedy, non-reliance or disclosure/knowledge provision limits liability for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment or dishonesty. This should apply to the Seller and to its knowledge of the Company's fraud.
- **Recommendation:** Insist on the carve-out as a non-negotiable. Contracting out of liability for your own fraud is generally unenforceable, and a silent draft invites argument.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation** (Priority: High)
- **Seller:** One regime for everything. "Claims" is undefined and broad, and limitations apply to "all Claims".
- **Buyer wants:** A liability schedule with distinct categories (general warranties; fundamental/title; tax; IP; specific indemnities; fraud), each with its own cap, thresholds and time limit. Specific indemnities should be pound-for-pound, outside the warranty cap and basket, and not reduced by disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Restructure the draft this way and define "Claims" narrowly. It is the structural fix that makes 001–005 workable.

## B. Disclosure and knowledge

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** (Priority: Critical)
- **Seller:** Everything in the data room (DD-002 to DD-012) is disclosed generally, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2). DL 1.4 adds blanket non-admissions.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific disclosure against specific warranties only. If general disclosure is conceded at all, it should cover only documents fairly disclosing the matter with reasonable detail, and exclude the data room at large and public registers. Disclosure should never qualify specific indemnities, title, tax or fraud. The Disclosure Letter's own statements that facts are "not established" should not be treated as disclosure of the consequences.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure. Combined with 007, it could reduce warranty protection to near zero.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** (Priority: Critical)
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3). DL item 11 adds that the Buyer "must evaluate the disclosed facts".
- **Buyer wants:** Delete cl 8.3. Add an express pro-buyer clause stating that Wattlebridge's rights are unaffected by any investigation or knowledge. At most, accept actual knowledge of named individuals, limited to matters specifically disclosed.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "discoverable" knowledge outright. It would convert due diligence into a waiver of claims.

## C. Conditions, debt and price mechanics

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** (Priority: Critical)
- **Seller:** Calls the consent "addressed". It offers reasonable endeavours and deems the condition satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL item 2 admits there is no final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (about 30%).
- **Buyer wants:** A Completion condition requiring unconditional written consent in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, with any cl 11.3 conditions satisfied or approved by the Buyer. The Buyer should hold the sole right to waive, and there should be a long-stop date with a termination right. Consider a price retention or earn-out linked to Bluefen retention.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the deeming wording. A conditional consent counted as satisfaction could leave Wattlebridge buying a business that has lost 30% of its revenue.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** (Priority: Critical)
- **Seller:** Release "following Completion" (cl 2/7). The facility is about AUD 3.2m outstanding and unpaid, with no discharge (DL item 3).
- **Buyer wants:** Repayment at Completion out of the price via the funds flow, against a payout letter. Discharge of security and PPSR deregistration should be delivered at Completion. Cl 8.1 change-control must be dealt with.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release. "Debt-free" means the Company is debt-free at Completion, and the Buyer should not carry security exposure.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** (Priority: High)
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 DD-005 closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow (DL item 5). On-costs are unstated.
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses treated as a transaction cost or debt-like item. They should be paid, or deducted from the price, at Completion, together with superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs, which should be quantified. Add a Seller indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Require inclusion in the funds flow. These are Company obligations triggered by Completion, so the Company, and so the Buyer, would otherwise bear them.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** (Priority: Medium)
- **Seller:** Calls the three renewals (AUD 110,000 each, AUD 330,000 in total) ordinary-course operating costs. DL item 8 does not say whether they are committed, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:** Confirmation of the status, term, termination rights and counterparties of each. Treat any pre-Completion commitment or prepayment as debt-like or a working-capital adjustment. Add an interim covenant that no renewals are signed without Buyer consent. Ask why three related renewals of identical amount exist (possible splitting).
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" label until the facts are verified. Amounts are modest, but this is cheap to resolve now.

## D. Specific risks

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** (Priority: High)
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment and is "adequate". DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, with no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room (DL item 4).
- **Buyer wants:** Payment of the AUD 180,000 as a Seller cost or from the funds flow. A confirmatory assignment of SOW3 Project Materials as a Completion deliverable. A broader indemnity for any loss from defective Company title to, or licence of, Ironquay-developed IP, including third-party claims. This should sit outside the cap and basket, with an IP ownership warranty.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the narrow indemnity. Paying the invoice does not resolve whether the Company owns the IP. I have not seen the existing indemnity wording, so please send it for review.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** (Priority: Critical)
- **Seller:** Calls DD-006 "preliminary" and "not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL item 6 says the file may contain about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Unauthorised access, scope and notification are not established, and no loss figure is given.
- **Buyer wants:** A specific indemnity, outside the cap and basket, for all losses from the incident (regulatory, notification, remediation, claims). Seller covenants to complete the investigation and meet any Privacy Act notification duties. Buyer access to forensic findings and conduct rights over regulator and customer communications. Consider a retention or escrow until the position is clear.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "not material" characterisation and require a specific indemnity. An assessment under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme has a 30-day clock. Given today's date (6 Nov 2026) against the 22 Sept data room cut-off, check whether it has run, and ask when the incident occurred.

## E. Title and open terms

**SPA-N-015: Title verification** (Priority: High)
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012. DL item 10 says this "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification".
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification: ASIC and PPSR searches, share issue and transfer history, the constitution, any shareholder agreement, options or encumbrances (including any Riverlark share charge). Completion deliverables should include executed transfers, resignations and resolutions. Add a fundamental title warranty.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the register alone. Make clean title a condition, and complete this work before signing.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** (Priority: High)
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime", with no separate terms.
- **Buyer wants:** A pre-Completion tax indemnity and tax warranties with a longer period, at least 5 years and aligned with ATO amendment periods. IP warranties covering ownership, employee and contractor assignments, open-source use and non-infringement, with a higher cap (up to 100% of price) and a longer period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the general regime. For a SaaS business, IP is the core value and tax liabilities can surface years later.

---

## Suggested next steps
1. Reply to Seller counsel that no position is treated as final and the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] labelling is not accepted.
2. Prepare the mark-up around a category-based liability schedule (014), and add the fraud carve-out (005) and deletion of cl 8.3 (007).
3. Run a Completion checklist: Bluefen consent, Riverlark payout and discharge, Ironquay assignment, title deliverables and the funds flow.
4. Send urgent information requests on the incident timeline and notification status, Bluefen cl 11.3, the Ironquay indemnity text and bonus on-costs, and the Sandbar contracts.
5. Raise whether the price needs adjustment or a retention for Bluefen, the bonuses and the incident.
=== END ADVICE ===
